content.title: 'Jumanji 4' Delayed to Christmas 2026 After 'Avengers: Doomsday' and 'Dune: Part Three'
content.text: 'Jumanji 4' Release Date Delayed Until After 'Avengers' & 'Dune' Sequels Kevin Hart, Karen Gillan, Jack Black, and Dwayne Johnson in Jumanji: Welcome to the JungleSony Pictures Releasing Published Mar 24, 2026, 3:10 PM EDT Richard Fink is a contributing writer in Los Angeles, California. Born in Phoenix, Arizona, Richard holds a Bachelor's Degree in Film and Media Production from ASU and has been writing professional about film and television since 2021. Movies have always been his passion, and he has a passion for history, comics, and cooking. Contact him at richardf@movieweb.com In a shocking move, Columbia Pictures is delaying the highly anticipated Jumanji sequel a few weeks to Christmas Day. Jumanji 4 is now headed to theaters just after the box office showdown between Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three, opening the same day as Robert Eggers Werwulf from Focus Features and an untitled biopic about running back John Tuggle distributed by Paramount Pictures. Jumanji 4 has been delayed from its original Dec. 11, 2026, release date to Dec. 25. The sequel will see Dwayne Johnson, Jack Black, Kevin Hart, Karen Gillan, Nick Jonas, and Danny DeVito, among many others, reprise their roles from the previous films. Jake Kasdan, who helmed both Welcome to the Jungle and The Next Level, returns as the director. This will mark the first Jumanji film in seven years, following the release of the 2019 sequel. Dwayne Johnson as Dr. Xander "Smolder" Bravestone and Kevin Hart as Franklin "Mouse" Finbar in Jumanji: The Next LevelSony Pictures Releasing The Jumanji franchise has proven to be a box office hit over the December holiday weekend. The original Jumanji, starring Robin Williams, opened on Dec. 15, 1995, and grossed $262.8 million worldwide. Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle became a surprise hit when it opened in theaters on Dec. 20, 2017. Managing to hold strong alongside Star Wars: The Last Jedi and The Greatest Showman, Welcome to the Jungle grossed $962 million worldwide, becoming the fifth highest-grossing film of the year. Jumanji: The Next Level opened in theaters on Dec. 13, 2019, and grossed $801 million, becoming the tenth highest-grossing film of the year. The decision to delay Jumanji 4 to Christmas Day is particularly shocking, as now the movie will come one week after Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three on Dec. 18, 2026. In a box office battle being labeled Dunesday, Dune: Part Three has already locked out Avengers: Doomsday from IMAX screens for three weeks. With two of the biggest movies of 2026 opening on the same weekend, the decision to move Jumanji 4 right into the middle of that action as opposed to getting out ahead of it and having a week to itself at the box office is head-scratching. Dec. 11 is now left without a major release, though Netflix's The Chronicles of Narnia by Greta Gerwig is expected to be released that weekend. Now the Jumanji franchise has proven it can co-exist alongside other December releases. Despite opening five days after Star Wars: The Last Jedi, Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle was a box office hit that showed incredible hold into January. The Next Level opened one week earlier than The Rise of Skywalker. Yet, Jumanji 4 is now jumping into the middle of a blockbuster showdown between two high-profile films, as well as into a post-COVID-19 pandemic film landscape. Jumanji: The Next Level was one of the last big box office hits before the COVID-19 pandemic shut down theaters, so there are a great many questions about whether, seven years later, the franchise still has the goods to bring audiences to the movies.
